data.title: Stifel Says Buy AMD Stock, Cites 'Durability of the EPYC Ramp'
data.description:

data.title: 3 Quantum Computing Stocks With a "Strong Buy" Rating, According to Analysts
data.description:

The company has been rolling out new systems and cloud tools, and its early commercial traction gives it a clear edge in the industry.

data.title: "This Slowdown Is Hard to Ignore," says UBS Analyst as NuScale Stock (SMR) Sinks 16% on Fresh Sell Call
data.description:
NuScale Power (SMR) shares tanked 16% after UBS analyst Jon Windham downgraded the stock to Sell and cut his price target to $6 (30.3% downside risk) from $10. The analyst said the company faces rising hurdles as other small modular reactor companies move ahead with real projects while its long build timeline and weak customer pipeline hold it back.

Windham lowered his price target to $6, using a 17x EV/cash EBITDA multiple on 2028 estimates. He also noted NuScale had $5 per share in net cash as of Q2 2026.

Why The Analyst Turned Bearish

Windham said NuScale's over 5-year build timeline and lack of firm customer deals make the road ahead tough. The analyst now assumes only one project will start construction in 2028 and expects about $700 million in cash burn from 2026 to 2028. 

Promotion

SMR has a long & short ETF? Explore SMU & SMZ

Revenue is expected to jump from $185 million in 2028 to $924 million in 2030, a huge growth rate, but earnings stay negative through 2030. He also said the market is pricing in $124 million of 2028 EBITDA, while the analyst's model shows only $29 million, leaving a big gap.

Falling Behind Rivals

The analyst said the small modular reactor industry has made major progress over the past four years, with several competitors already moving into construction:

  • GE‑Hitachi is building an SMR in Canada, and the TVA has filed a construction permit for a GE‑Hitachi unit.
  • 4G Nuclear is also making clear progress with new funding and project launches.

Windham expects only 2-4 advanced SMR designs to scale for commercial power. With rivals already at or near construction and NuScale still years away, he sees the path forward as "increasingly difficult."

Concerns Around ENTRA1 Partnership

The analyst also flagged risk in NuScale's ENTRA1 partnership, which requires NuScale to make upfront payments for non‑binding customer deals. He sees a real chance the TVA may not move forward with NuScale. If TVA does proceed, the analyst estimated that 2.8 GW of potential projects could trigger $1.4 billion in extra payments to ENTRA1.

Is SMR Stock a Good Buy?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Hold consensus rating on NuScale stock based on five Buys, seven Holds, and two Sells assigned in the past three months. Further, the average SMR price target of $11.32 per share implies 31.45% upside potential.

data.title: Tesla Stock (TSLA): Top Morgan Stanley Analyst Sees Strong Upside in Autonomous Trucking Plans
data.description:
Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Percoco kept a Hold on Tesla (TSLA) stock and a $400 price target. The five-star analyst said the long‑term case for Tesla's autonomous trucking business remains strong. Percoco pointed to new work from the bank's freight team, which sees autonomous trucking as a major shift for the industry. After nearly ten years of tech development, the focus is now moving toward commercial rollout over the next 12-18 months. The team's updated numbers show a huge market, with a U.S. total addressable market of $0.5 trillion to $1.1 trillion by 2041.

The analyst said the economics also look strong. Autonomous trucks could cut net costs by about 20%, mainly from lower labor, fuel, and insurance costs. That means an autonomous fleet could earn 6-8 times more profit than today's human‑driven fleets.

It is worth noting that Percoco ranks 187th out of more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. He has an overall success rate of 61%, with an average return per rating of 56.8% over a one-year timeframe.

data.title: OKLO Stock Tanked Over 9% on Friday – Here's What Spooked Investors
data.description:
Oklo (OKLO) shares fell over 9% on Friday after the company rolled out a new $1 billion at‑the‑market (ATM) equity offering, raising fresh dilution concerns among investors. The raise gives Oklo more funding for its future small modular nuclear reactors.

The company announced a deal with ten sales agents, including Goldman Sachs (GS), BofA Securities, Citigroup (C), J.P. Morgan (JPM), Morgan Stanley (MS), Barclays (BCS), Cantor Fitzgerald, Guggenheim, Canaccord Genuity, and B. Riley. Each agent can earn up to a 1.5% fee on the gross price of every share sold.

Why the Offering Pulled the Stock Down

The size and timing of the offering hit sentiment hard. Oklo just finished using its previous $1 billion ATM program, launched in May. The company sold 17.97 million shares in only four months. The company is issuing new shares again, which adds fresh dilution risk for current shareholders.

Promotion

METQ: built for a short position on META

If Oklo sells the full $1 billion at prices near $40, it would need to issue about 25 million new shares. That means about 11.5% dilution for current holders, a clear short‑term negative because each existing share would represent a smaller slice of the company.

Piper Sandler Analyst Bullish on OKLO Stock

The drop comes just days after upbeat analyst coverage. Piper Sandler analyst Dimple Gosai started coverage with a Buy rating and a $55 price target, pointing to strong long‑term demand for nuclear power from AI data centers.

The analyst noted that nuclear power is getting strong support from both parties in Washington and from big tech firms that need steady, clean energy, as shown by Meta's (META) recent deal. In Gosai's view, Oklo is one of the few fully built‑out nuclear developers that can meet this fast‑rising AI power demand as the industry moves closer to real commercial rollout.

What is OKLO's Price Target?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on Oklo stock based on seven Buys and six Holds assigned in the past three months. Further, the average Oklo price target of $72.83 per share implies 101.09% upside potential.

data.title: J.P. Morgan Assigns Hims & Hers Stock a 'Hold' Rating. What's Behind the Cautious Stance?
data.description:
J.P. Morgan analyst Bryan Smilek initiated coverage of telehealth platform Hims & Hers Health (HIMS) with a Hold rating and a price target of $32. The analyst is positive about the company's vertical integration, brand scale, and expansion across specialties and geographies. However, Smilek currently prefers to be on the sidelines as he looks for "execution across the strategic transition toward branded GLP-1s, durability of growth across newer specialties, deeper int'l penetration, & durable margin expansion."

J.P. Morgan Is Cautious on HIMS Stock

Smilek noted that Hims & Hers Health's five specialties (such as the GLP-1/weight loss business) generate more than $100 million in annual U.S. revenue, while three international markets (UK, Australia, and Germany) also generate over $100 million in annualized revenue. He highlighted that HIMS continues to rapidly expand its hormonal offerings for both men and women, as well as its Labs offerings.

Furthermore, the analyst noted that while most of the GLP-1 business was historically based on compounding treatments, HIMS announced a strategic shift in March under which the U.S. weight loss business will focus more on branded, FDA-approved treatments. While HIMS will no longer advertise compounded GLP-1 offerings, it will still offer them where clinically required.

data.title: Tesla (TSLA) to Bring Its Semi Electric Truck to Europe in 2027
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) has confirmed that its Semi electric truck is coming to Europe, with customer deliveries set to begin in 2027. The EV giant introduced the adapted European model at the IAA Transportation show in Hannover. It also launched new regional web pages with the truck's specs, design updates, and key features.

The move marks Tesla's first big push for the Semi outside North America. The truck was first shown in 2017, but production faced long delays as Tesla focused battery supplies on its passenger cars. Limited U.S. deliveries began in late 2022, and Tesla said earlier this year that the first Semi had rolled off a high‑volume line in Nevada. Full production is now planned for 2026.

Tesla's European site lists a version with up to 550 km of range at a 40‑tonne weight, using about 1 kWh per kilometer. The truck weighs around 9,100 kg without cargo and offers 25 kW of electric power take‑off. Using Tesla's Megacharger network, the Semi can recover about 60% of its range in 30 minutes, with charging speeds up to 800 kW.

Promotion

TSLQ: built for a short position on TSLA

Tesla said the European Semi will come with route‑based charging plans and its own service centers to reduce downtime for fleet operators. The launch puts Tesla into a fast-growing European truck market where several truck makers already sell battery-powered heavy-duty models.

Key Details About Tesla Semi

The Tesla Semi is built as a Class 8 electric truck that beats standard diesel trucks in efficiency, running costs, and hill‑climbing power. The Semi uses a multi‑motor setup where one "torque axle" gives strong low‑speed power for pulling heavy loads uphill, and a second "efficiency axle" helps the truck cruise smoothly on highways.

The truck replaced old hydraulic assist with a fully electric power steering system. It maintains a physical link to the wheels. However, the setup gives a smoother steering feel and makes it easier to tie in Autopilot features.

Data from hundreds of pilot trucks that have logged over 13.5 million miles reflect the vehicle's advantages. During commercial freight testing, the Semi averaged an energy consumption of 1.55 to 1.7 kWh per mile at steady highway speeds. Thanks to its strong efficiency and low drag (about 0.4), the Semi is roughly 50% cheaper to run per mile than diesel trucks in high fuel-cost states like California, and about 20% cheaper nationwide.

Is Tesla Stock Good to Buy Now?

Turning to Wall Street, TSLA stock has a Hold consensus rating based on 11 Buys, 12 Holds, and three Sells assigned in the past three months. The average price target for Tesla is $377.08, implying a 3.18% upside from the current price.

data.title: September Rate Hike Odds Surge Above 85% as Inflation Accelerates
data.description:
Rate hike odds at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting surged on Friday after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) published August's Consumer Price Index (CPI) data. During the month, the CPI rose 0.4%, up from 0.1% in July. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy items, advanced 0.3% compared to 0.2% in the prior month.

The odds of a 25-basis-point hike next week are now at 88.7%, up from 72.4% on Thursday and 59.4% a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Fed Faces Balancing Act as Inflation Stays Elevated

Inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% target for over five years. Higher rates can help ease inflation by increasing borrowing costs and discouraging consumers and companies from spending.
